quiz.title: Class 12 Matrices Mock Test (15 Minutes)
quiz.intro: Eight mixed matrices questions at CBSE Class 12 level. Give yourself about 15 minutes, pick an answer for each, then press Check my score and read the working.
quiz.about: Class 12 matrices: order, operations, multiplication, transpose, symmetric and skew-symmetric, inverse and elementary operations

questions.q: A matrix has 3 rows and 5 columns. What is its order and how many elements does it have?
questions.explanation: Order is written rows × columns, so 3 × 5. The number of elements is the product 3 × 5 = 15.

questions.q: Which product of matrices is defined?
questions.explanation: The product AB is defined only when the number of columns of A equals the number of rows of B. A 3×2 times a 2×4 matches (2 = 2) and gives a 3×4 matrix.
Row 1 of A times columns of B: (1·0 + 2·1, 1·1 + 2·0) = (2, 1). Row 2: (3·0 + 4·1, 3·1 + 4·0) = (4, 3). So AB = [[2, 1], [4, 3]].

questions.q: For A = [[2, -1], [3, 5]], what is the transpose A'?
questions.explanation: The transpose swaps rows and columns: the first row (2, -1) becomes the first column, giving A' = [[2, 3], [-1, 5]].

questions.q: A square matrix A is skew-symmetric. What can be said about its diagonal entries?
options: They are all equal to each other but non-zero
They equal the corresponding entries of A'
questions.explanation: Skew-symmetric means A' = -A, so each diagonal entry satisfies a = -a, which forces a = 0. Every diagonal element of a skew-symmetric matrix is zero.

questions.q: For A = [[3, 5], [1, 2]], what is A inverse?
questions.explanation: det A = 3·2 - 5·1 = 1. For a 2×2 matrix the inverse is (1/det) times [[d, -b], [-c, a]] = [[2, -5], [-1, 3]].

questions.q: Applying the elementary row operation R2 → R2 - 2R1 to A = [[1, 3], [2, 5]] gives which matrix?
questions.explanation: New R2 = (2 - 2·1, 5 - 2·3) = (0, -1). R1 is unchanged, so the result is [[1, 3], [0, -1]].

faq.q: How long should the Class 12 matrices mock test take?
faq.a: Aim for about 15 minutes for the eight questions, roughly two minutes each. Matrices work rewards care over speed, so check your row-by-column products before moving on rather than rushing.

faq.q: When is the product of two matrices defined?
faq.a: The product AB exists only when the number of columns of A equals the number of rows of B. A p×q matrix times a q×r matrix gives a p×r result; if the inner numbers do not match, the product is undefined.

faq.q: What is the difference between a symmetric and a skew-symmetric matrix?
faq.a: A symmetric matrix satisfies A' = A, so entries mirror across the diagonal. A skew-symmetric matrix satisfies A' = -A, which forces every diagonal entry to be zero. Any square matrix can be written as the sum of a symmetric and a skew-symmetric part.

faq.q: How do you find the inverse of a 2×2 matrix?
faq.a: For A = [[a, b], [c, d]], first find det A = ad - bc. If it is non-zero, the inverse is (1/det A) times [[d, -b], [-c, a]]. A matrix with zero determinant is singular and has no inverse.
